playbook:
When I am dealt K and I act first, I bet to extract value and apply pressure.
When I am dealt K and my opponent checks to me, I bet for value rather than giving a free showdown.
When my opponent bets and I hold K, I continue (call) — do not fold a King to a single-unit bet; treat it as value and contest.
When I am dealt Q and I act first, I usually open with a bet to take the initiative and get value.
When I am dealt Q and my opponent checks to me, I usually bet to steal or build value; I will mix in occasional checks to avoid being exploitable.
When my opponent bets and I hold Q, I call modest single-unit bets to contest the pot; fold only to very large pressure or repeated evidence the opponent never bluffs.
When I am dealt J and I act first, I check (do not bluff too often from the worst card).
When my opponent bets and I hold J, I generally call small single-unit bets to keep the pot contested; fold if pot odds or opponent behavior make calling clearly unprofitable.
When I am behind in match equity (chip deficit), shift to more aggression: bet K more insistently and increase betting frequency with Q to apply pressure and try to recover chips; still avoid over-bluffing with J.
When I am ahead in match equity, favor straightforward value betting with K and Q and avoid unnecessary bluffs with J.
When the opponent checks and I have a marginal hand (J or sometimes Q in a risky spot), prefer checking to avoid being exploited.
Mixing: introduce occasional deviations from the above (checking some K or betting some J very rarely) to remain unpredictable, but keep those deviations infrequent.
Always declare my card truthfully at showdown.
